answer: AI document processing, also called intelligent document processing, uses AI to read documents such as invoices, forms and PDFs, identify the information that matters, extract it as structured data and send it to your business systems. Unlike older OCR templates, it copes with different layouts and messy scans.
body:
The hidden cost of re-keying documents

Every business has a pile of documents someone has to read and type into a system: supplier invoices into the accounts package, application forms into a CRM, delivery dockets into a job system, signed contracts into a register. The work is slow, boring and error-prone, and mistakes surface later as wrong payments, missed deadlines or compliance gaps. AI document processing takes over the reading and typing, and leaves people to check the cases that genuinely need judgement.

Documents we process

DocumentData extractedWhere it goes
Supplier invoices and billsSupplier, ABN, invoice number, dates, line items, GST, totalsDraft bills in Xero or MYOB
Receipts and expensesMerchant, date, amount, GST, categoryExpense claims and accounting software
Application and intake formsNames, contact details, answers, signaturesCRM, practice or case management systems
Purchase orders and docketsItems, quantities, prices, delivery detailsERP, inventory or job systems
Contracts and agreementsParties, dates, renewal terms, key clausesContract register with reminders
Emails and attachmentsRequest type, customer, urgency, reference numbersHelpdesk, CRM or the right inbox

How AI document processing works

  1. Capture: documents arrive by email, upload, scan or from a shared folder.
  2. Read: AI reads text and layout, including scanned and photographed documents.
  3. Extract: the fields you need are pulled out as structured data.
  4. Validate: rules check the data, for example that the ABN format is valid, GST adds up, the supplier exists and the invoice isn’t a duplicate.
  5. Route: clean documents are filed automatically; anything with low confidence or a failed check goes to a person with the issue highlighted.
  6. Log: every document has a record of what was extracted, checked and filed, with the original attached.

Why AI beats template OCR

Older OCR tools needed a template for every supplier and broke whenever a layout changed. AI models understand documents more like a person does: they find the invoice total whether it sits at the top, bottom or in a table, and they can read new suppliers without set-up. That means far less maintenance and higher automation rates as volumes grow.

Accuracy and human review

No extraction system is perfect, so we design for checking. Each field carries a confidence score, validation rules catch inconsistencies, and anything below your threshold is sent for review in a simple screen that shows the document beside the extracted data. Your team approves or corrects in seconds, and corrections help us tune the system. Payments are never released without the approval rules you already use.

Privacy and security for sensitive documents

Documents often contain personal, financial or health information. We process them in secure environments, use Australian hosting regions where the platform offers them, limit who can see originals, and set retention periods with you. Our design follows the Privacy Act 1988 and the OAIC’s guidance on commercially available AI products, and we configure AI providers so your documents aren’t used to train public models where that option exists.

Where document processing fits

Document processing is usually one stage of a bigger process, such as procure-to-pay or client onboarding. We often deliver it as part of business process automation, with workflows handling the steps before and after. For accounting firms and bookkeepers, see AI for accounting.

How a document processing project runs

  1. Free AI audit to look at your document types and volumes.
  2. Sample testing: we run a set of your real documents through the system and report accuracy before you commit.
  3. Build: capture, extraction, validation, routing and review screens, usually two to four weeks.
  4. Supervised launch: your team reviews output closely for the first weeks.
  5. Monthly reporting on documents processed, automation rate and exceptions.

Common starting points are accounts payable invoices, new client intake forms and supplier delivery dockets, because they arrive in high volumes, follow recognisable patterns and are easy to measure. Once the first document type is running, adding the next usually takes days rather than weeks.

We report the automation rate each month, so you can see exactly how many documents were filed without anyone touching them.
faqs: Can AI read scanned or photographed documents?
Yes. Modern AI models read scans and phone photos as well as digital PDFs. Very poor images may need a person to check them, and the system flags those automatically.
Does AI document processing work with Xero and MYOB?
Yes. Extracted invoices and receipts can be created as draft bills or expense entries in Xero or MYOB, with the original document attached and GST and ABN details checked.
How accurate is AI document extraction?
Accuracy depends on document quality and variety. We test on a sample of your own documents before you commit, and every field below your confidence threshold is sent to a person for review.
What happens to our documents after processing?

Originals and extracted data are stored in your systems with retention periods you choose. We use secure processing, Australian hosting regions where available and AI settings that keep your data out of public model training.
